subject: Livechat delivery slowdown — recovery summary & remediation plan
messages:
From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@greenshelf.co>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Livechat slowdown this morning — urgent

Rishi,

We started seeing a pronounced slowdown in our live customer chat responses starting ~07:55 PDT this morning. Users reported messages taking 6–12s to get the first token back (previous baseline ~200–400ms). It impacts our live agent handoff flow and our satisfaction metrics.

What we have observed on our side:
- Spike in COMET_CONNECT errors around 07:56, followed by long tails on response first-byte times.
- No changes on our client config (same SDK version).
- We temporarily toggled to polling (non-streaming) and latency improved but throughput dropped.

Can you confirm if anything on Redwood’s side is ongoing? We need an ETA and immediate mitigations we can apply. I can share logs and a short trace if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Huang
Product Ops — GreenShelf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Livechat slowdown this morning — urgent

Alex — thanks for flagging this and for the trace file. We’re looking into it now. Quick operational notes and immediate actions you can try while we triage:

1) Short-term client workarounds you can enable immediately
- Switch to our non-streaming/fetch path when you detect >2s first-byte (you already tried this and saw better latency).
- Reduce max_tokens_per_chunk to 128 for live sessions (helps keep per-request kernel selection predictable).
- Enable a 400–600ms client-side read timeout fallback to force quick reconnects rather than long slow reads.

2) Configuration checks on your SDK
- Confirm you are on SDK v3.4.1+ (there was a connection pooling improvement in 3.4.0 that reduces long-tail TTFB).
- If you have keep-alive disabled in your proxy, re-enable it (we’ve seen long TCP teardown affecting first-byte on some corp proxies).

3) What we’re doing now
- I’ve escalated to infra and runtime (cc’d laura and sergio). We’re checking node-level telemetry, prefix cache health, and any routing shifts.
- If helpful, share an example request-id from a slow trace (X-Redwood-Request-Id in your CSV) and we’ll pick up the full server trace.

We’ll follow up within the hour with a preliminary root cause or mitigation. If this is blocking a live campaign, tell us and we can prioritize a temporary capacity bump for your account.

— Rishi

We’re okay applying the client timeouts and reducing chunk size; please confirm if there are any server-side toggles you plan to apply so we don’t overlap changes. We are running a time-limited promotion through 18:00 PT so any restoration of normal behavior sooner is critical.

Also requesting a post-incident writeup and any compensatory credits if the root cause is on Redwood.

Alex

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@greenshelf.co>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident update: what happened, immediate remediation, and next steps

Alex / GreenShelf ops team — thank you for your patience while we completed the investigation. Summary and actions below.

Executive summary
- Incident window: 2027-04-20T07:55:00-07:00 to ~2027-04-20T10:40:00-07:00 (service restored gradually, some residual slow tails cleared after autoscaling warm-up).
- Impact: elevated first-byte latency for streaming/live-response endpoints resulting in slower interactive replies (observed 3–12s in affected requests).
- Root cause (short): an unexpected combination of a kernel scheduling regression in a recently deployed runtime patch + an atypical distribution of long-sequence requests that stressed prefix cache miss rates on a subset of US edge nodes. The regression increased per-request scheduling jitter for streaming paths, amplifying the cache miss impact.

What we did (immediate remediation)
- Rolled back the recent runtime patch that changed kernel scheduling heuristics (09:42 PDT) which removed the added jitter.
- Forced a targeted reprovisioning of the affected edge shard pool and primed prefix caches with a warm-up pass (09:58 PDT) to reduce miss rate for the long-sequence workload.
- Enabled a temporary routing override to route GreenShelf traffic to healthy nodes while the edge pool recovered (this was in effect until 10:40 PDT).

Customer-visible mitigations we recommended (and which you implemented)
- Temporary switch from streaming to non-streaming for critical flows while we rolled back.
- Lowered chunk sizing to 128 tokens for live sessions.
- Applied a client-side stale-read timeout to accelerate reconnects for long-tail connections.

Follow-up actions (longer-term)
- Revert has been followed by a new canary plan: we’ll gate kernel scheduling changes behind a targeted workload canary and an automated long-tail latency test. (Owner: Runtime — laura_bennett, ETA: 2027-05-12)
- Improve prefix cache telemetry and add an automated priming step during scale events to avoid cold misses for bursty long-sequence workloads. (Owner: Serving infra — sergio_alvarez, ETA: 2027-06-01)
- Provide a client-side best-practices note specific to live-response products: SDK version recommendation (>=3.4.1), chunk-sizing guidance, and socket keepalive settings. We’ll share a short KB in the next 72 hours. (Owner: Customer Success / DX, ETA: 2027-04-25)

Compensation and next steps
- We will apply a one-time credit for the impacted hours on your account (details to follow via billing).
- Attached is a concise incident summary and the connection traces we used for analysis.

Attachments:
- incident_summary_INC-20270420.pdf (concise timeline, root cause analysis, evidence)
- greenshelf_connection_traces_20270420.csv (redacted request ids used in analysis)

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute postmortem walk-through with engineering this week to go deeper into the traces and talk about SDK mitigations. Please let me know preferred times.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know this coincided with your promotion window and we’ll prioritize minimizing recurrence.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
